proposed_manuscript_claim: Pre-split synthetic oversampling (SMOTE) inflates cross-validation discrimination metrics through data leakage across evaluation folds.
underlying_result: Pre-split SMOTE reported ROC-AUC=0.9664 for XGBoost and 0.9187 for RandomForest, whereas clean training-only SMOTE achieved ROC-AUC=0.8098 and 0.8236 (artifactual inflation of +0.1566 and +0.0951 AUC).
statistical_evidence: Statistically significant difference (p < 0.0001) across 5 folds and held-out test set.
limitations_and_qualifications: Evaluated specifically on tabular nearest-neighbor interpolation in BRFSS; demonstrates severe vulnerability of unpartitioned resampling.

proposed_manuscript_claim: Clean training-only SMOTE degrades probability calibration without improving true rank-order discrimination compared to unresampled gradient boosted trees.
underlying_result: Unresampled XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC=0.8371, PR-AUC=0.3455, and Brier score=0.0657. Training-only 1:1 SMOTE decreased ROC-AUC to 0.8098, decreased PR-AUC to 0.2894, and increased Brier error to 0.0907 (+38.1% error increase).
statistical_evidence: Brier score increase from 0.0657 to 0.0907 is statistically significant (delta = +0.0250, z = -51.82, p < 0.0001).
limitations_and_qualifications: Synthetic interpolation creates unrealistic probability assignments in feature regions; threshold-moving on unresampled probabilities achieves screening goals without probability distortion.

proposed_manuscript_claim: The frozen 2020 unresampled XGBoost model maintains discriminative ranking when externally evaluated on independent out-of-time surveillance waves from 2021 and 2022.
underlying_result: ROC-AUC was 0.8371 in 2020 test, 0.8407 in 2021 external wave, and 0.8397 in 2022 external wave. PR-AUC was 0.3455 in 2020, 0.3304 in 2021, and 0.3501 in 2022.
statistical_evidence: Two-sample independent difference tests show zero statistically significant degradation (Delta AUC = +0.0036, 95% CI [-0.0049, +0.0121], p=0.407 for 2021; Delta AUC = +0.0026, 95% CI [-0.0061, +0.0113], p=0.560 for 2022).
limitations_and_qualifications: Evaluated strictly within the ongoing BRFSS surveillance system; does not imply external transportability to clinical inpatient or EHR cohorts.

proposed_manuscript_claim: A domain-informed decision threshold frozen on training cross-validation achieves approximately 80% screening sensitivity across multi-year temporal waves.
underlying_result: At frozen threshold tau=0.0816, unweighted sensitivity was 79.78% in 2020 test, 80.68% in 2021, and 81.96% in 2022, with specificity 73.09%, 72.24%, and 70.87%.
statistical_evidence: Point estimates remain stable within +/- 2.0% of the nominal 80% screening target across hundreds of thousands of independent respondents.
limitations_and_qualifications: Applies to unweighted respondent-level screening; survey-weighted sensitivity is moderately lower (~75.2%-78.7%) due to demographic post-stratification reweighting.

proposed_manuscript_claim: Accounting for BRFSS complex survey sampling weights results in lower population-weighted sensitivity and higher population-weighted specificity than unweighted metrics.
underlying_result: In 2021: weighted sensitivity is 75.19% (vs 80.68% unweighted) and weighted specificity is 80.17% (vs 72.24% unweighted). In 2022: weighted sensitivity is 78.72% (vs 81.96%) and specificity is 78.79% (vs 70.87%). Weighted ROC-AUC is 0.8564 in 2021 and 0.8607 in 2022.
statistical_evidence: Taylor series linearization standard errors (accounting for strata _STSTR and cluster _PSU) confirm significant shifts (DEFF ~ 1.76-4.38).
limitations_and_qualifications: Reflects CDC raking down-weighting over-represented elderly respondents (high recall ~93%) and up-weighting younger respondents (high specificity ~97%).

proposed_manuscript_claim: Age-related performance differences involve both within-group ranking discrimination degradation in elderly populations and severe operating threshold disparities across age strata.
underlying_result: ROC-AUC drops from ~0.795 in young (<50) to ~0.735-0.741 in elderly (70+). At the same fixed threshold tau=0.0816, sensitivity is ~31%-34% in young vs ~93% in elderly, while specificity is ~96%-97% in young vs ~29%-32% in elderly.
statistical_evidence: Within-group AUC degradation of ~0.06 is statistically significant (p < 0.0001); sensitivity disparity is 3.0-fold across an 11-fold prevalence gradient (1.6% to 19.2%).
limitations_and_qualifications: Demonstrates a dual phenomenon (discrimination drop AND threshold disparity). Age-specific thresholds are not automatically recommended without prospective clinical utility validation.

proposed_manuscript_claim: Self-reported behavioral lifestyle features (diet, exercise, alcohol, smoking, BMI) contribute substantially less discriminative power than age and self-reported general health.
underlying_result: Demographic features alone achieve ROC-AUC=0.7603. Adding General Health increases AUC to 0.826. All remaining behavioral lifestyle factors add only +0.011 AUC over demographics and health status.
statistical_evidence: Permutation importance confirms AgeCategory (drop=0.1127) and GenHealth (drop=0.0331) account for the vast majority of predictive attribution; lifestyle features drop AUC by <0.0015 individually.
limitations_and_qualifications: Reflects coarse categorical single-item survey measurement limitations in BRFSS, not biological or clinical irrelevance of lifestyle factors.

proposed_manuscript_claim: The pipeline is strictly a retrospective cross-sectional survey status classifier and must NOT be interpreted as a prospective clinical risk calculator or causal model.
underlying_result: Target _MICHD reflects lifetime self-reported diagnosis; survey respondents are surviving community dwellers; cross-sectional data cannot establish event temporality.
statistical_evidence: Epidemiological survey construction boundaries (CDC BRFSS documentation).
limitations_and_qualifications: Absolute methodological boundary for all manuscript claims; zero prospective risk or causal intervention claims permitted.

proposed_manuscript_claim: Complete-case evaluation retains >76% of survey respondents with minimal target prevalence selection bias but moderate demographic selection among excluded respondents.
underlying_result: Complete-case retention was 79.46% in 2021 (N=348,568) and 76.22% in 2022 (N=339,264). Target prevalence differed by only 0.11% in 2021 (8.16% vs 8.05%) and -0.50% in 2022 (8.92% vs 9.42%).
statistical_evidence: Excluded respondents have slightly higher representation of females (+7.4% to +8.5%) and racial minorities (+5.0% to +5.5%) due to item non-response on BMI and alcohol frequency.
limitations_and_qualifications: Renormalizing survey weights among complete cases does not completely eliminate item non-response selection; must be reported as a study limitation.

proposed_manuscript_claim: The 2021 SleepTime rotation was effectively addressed via a predefined 2020 training-derived median imputation rule (7.0 hours), whereas 2022 had 100% empirical measurement.
underlying_result: Imputing SleepTime=7.0 in 2021 preserved pristine calibration (ECE=0.0055, ROC-AUC=0.8407), whereas native NaN tree routing caused probability drift (ECE=0.0514, specificity=58.74%). In 2022, 100% empirical measurement achieved ROC-AUC=0.8397 and ECE=0.0044.
statistical_evidence: Empirical validation across two separate survey waves with different feature availability modes.
limitations_and_qualifications: The median imputation rule was derived strictly from 2020 development data prior to 2021 evaluation; native NaN routing is retained as a sensitivity benchmark.
